chunks.text: Cache Digitech Pvt. Ltd is a leading System Integration, Consulting and IT Infrastructure company with over three decades of experience. Core offerings include IT Infrastructure, Cloud, Cybersecurity, Data & AI, Managed Services, Consulting, Networking, and Telecom solutions.

chunks.title: Which cloud platforms does Cache Digitech work with?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Cloud platforms Question: Which cloud platforms does Cache Digitech work with? Answer: The Cache Digitech website identifies AWS, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud Platform (GCP) within its cloud offering. Confirm current partner status, supported services and limitations with the cloud team.

chunks.title: What is cloud rehosting or lift-and-shift migration?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Migration Question: What is cloud rehosting or lift-and-shift migration? Answer: Rehosting moves a workload to cloud infrastructure with limited application changes. It may accelerate migration, but does not automatically modernize or optimize the application.

chunks.title: What is the difference between rehosting and replatforming?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Migration Question: What is the difference between rehosting and replatforming? Answer: Rehosting moves an application with minimal changes. Replatforming makes selected changes to use cloud capabilities without fully redesigning the application.

chunks.title: What should be included in a cloud migration assessment?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Migration Question: What should be included in a cloud migration assessment? Answer: Common areas include workload inventory, dependencies, security, compliance, target architecture, migration options, cost estimates, risks and sequencing. Confirm the formal assessment scope with the cloud team.

chunks.title: How can application dependencies be identified before migration?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Migration Question: How can application dependencies be identified before migration? Answer: Inventory applications, databases, integrations, network paths, identity dependencies and upstream/downstream services. Dependency mapping helps group workloads into migration waves.

chunks.title: How can cloud migration downtime be reduced?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Migration Question: How can cloud migration downtime be reduced? Answer: Use dependency planning, replication where suitable, rehearsal, phased migration, cutover validation and a tested rollback plan. Downtime commitments must be validated for each workload.

chunks.title: What is a cloud landing zone?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Architecture Question: What is a cloud landing zone? Answer: A landing zone is a governed cloud foundation that typically includes identity, network design, logging, security policies, account structure and baseline automation.

chunks.title: What is hybrid cloud?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Architecture Question: What is hybrid cloud? Answer: Hybrid cloud combines on-premises or private-cloud infrastructure with public cloud services. Design depends on latency, data handling, security, resilience and operations.

chunks.title: What is multi-cloud management?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Architecture Question: What is multi-cloud management? Answer: Multi-cloud management coordinates operations, governance and cost visibility across more than one cloud provider. Confirm which management functions are included in the proposed service.

chunks.title: What is cloud-native modernization?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Architecture Question: What is cloud-native modernization? Answer: Cloud-native modernization adapts applications to use suitable capabilities such as containers, managed services, microservices or serverless components.

chunks.title: What are microservices?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Architecture Question: What are microservices? Answer: Microservices structure an application as smaller services that can be developed and deployed independently. They can improve release flexibility but introduce distributed-system complexity.

chunks.title: What is serverless computing?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Architecture Question: What is serverless computing? Answer: Serverless lets teams run code or services without managing underlying servers directly. Design should account for runtime limits, cost, security and service dependencies.

chunks.title: What is Kubernetes and when is it useful?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Architecture Question: What is Kubernetes and when is it useful? Answer: Kubernetes orchestrates containerized applications, including scheduling, scaling and service recovery. It is useful for suitable container workloads but adds operational complexity.

chunks.title: When should an enterprise use containers?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Architecture Question: When should an enterprise use containers? Answer: Containers package applications and dependencies consistently across environments. Suitability depends on portability needs, deployment patterns, isolation and operational capability.

chunks.title: How should workloads be placed across cloud and on-premises?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Architecture Question: How should workloads be placed across cloud and on-premises? Answer: Consider latency, data residency, security, licensing, resilience, integration, performance and total cost. Validate workload placement against the target architecture.

chunks.title: What is cloud governance?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Governance Question: What is cloud governance? Answer: Cloud governance defines policies, roles and guardrails for identity, security, approved services, tagging, cost ownership and compliance evidence.

chunks.title: What is policy-as-code?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Governance Question: What is policy-as-code? Answer: Policy-as-code expresses governance or security rules in machine-readable form so they can be checked consistently during provisioning and operations.

chunks.title: How can an enterprise manage cloud sprawl?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Governance Question: How can an enterprise manage cloud sprawl? Answer: Use resource inventory, account governance, tagging, approved provisioning patterns, lifecycle policies and ownership reviews.

chunks.title: How can cloud resources be tagged consistently?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Governance Question: How can cloud resources be tagged consistently? Answer: Define required tags such as application, owner, environment, cost centre and lifecycle. Apply validation at provisioning and monitor non-compliant resources.

chunks.title: How should cloud access be controlled?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Security Question: How should cloud access be controlled? Answer: Use least-privilege roles, strong authentication, centralized identity, periodic access reviews and monitored privileged access.

chunks.title: What is cloud security posture management?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Security Question: What is cloud security posture management? Answer: Cloud security posture management identifies cloud misconfigurations and policy deviations. Exact capabilities depend on tools, platforms and integrations.

chunks.title: How can cloud data be protected?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Security Question: How can cloud data be protected? Answer: Use suitable identity controls, encryption, key management, network restrictions, backups, logging and data classification based on data sensitivity and risk.

chunks.title: What is cloud monitoring?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Operations Question: What is cloud monitoring? Answer: Cloud monitoring collects metrics, logs and events to show service health, performance, capacity and availability. Alerts should have clear owners and runbooks.

chunks.title: How should cloud backup and disaster recovery be designed?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Operations Question: How should cloud backup and disaster recovery be designed? Answer: Identify critical workloads, recovery time objectives, recovery point objectives, retention, isolation and restoration testing. Targets should be agreed and tested.

chunks.title: What is cloud workload right-sizing?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Optimization Question: What is cloud workload right-sizing? Answer: Right-sizing adjusts compute, memory or other resources to match observed demand. Changes must be validated against performance, resilience and growth requirements.

chunks.title: What is FinOps?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: FinOps Question: What is FinOps? Answer: FinOps is a collaborative operating practice that connects engineering, finance and business teams to understand cloud spend and balance cost, performance and value.

chunks.title: What does a cloud cost assessment examine?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: FinOps Question: What does a cloud cost assessment examine? Answer: It may review spend trends, resource utilization, idle assets, commitments, storage, data transfer, tagging and ownership. Findings should use the customer's billing and usage data.

chunks.title: How can cloud costs be allocated to business units?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: FinOps Question: How can cloud costs be allocated to business units? Answer: Use consistent tags, accounts or subscriptions, shared-cost rules and reporting by application, team or cost centre.

chunks.title: What are reserved instances or savings plans?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: FinOps Question: What are reserved instances or savings plans? Answer: These are provider-specific commitment models that may reduce rates in exchange for usage or spend commitments. Assess demand stability and utilization risk first.

chunks.title: How can idle cloud resources be identified?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: FinOps Question: How can idle cloud resources be identified? Answer: Use inventory and usage data to identify low-utilization resources, then verify ownership and dependencies before resizing or decommissioning them.

chunks.title: Can cloud cost savings be guaranteed?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: FinOps Question: Can cloud cost savings be guaranteed? Answer: Savings depend on the current environment, usage, pricing, architecture and approved changes. Any numerical or guaranteed claim must be confirmed with Cache Digitech before publication.

chunks.title: Does Cache Digitech offer a cloud cost assessment?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Commercial Question: Does Cache Digitech offer a cloud cost assessment? Answer: The cloud page advertises a complimentary 14-day cloud cost assessment. Confirm current eligibility, included scope, access requirements and terms before publishing this offer.

chunks.title: How is cloud migration pricing determined?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Commercial Question: How is cloud migration pricing determined? Answer: Pricing depends on workload complexity, target architecture, data volumes, migration windows, testing, licensing and post-migration support.

chunks.title: Can Cache Digitech manage billing across multiple clouds?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Commercial Question: Can Cache Digitech manage billing across multiple clouds? Answer: The website describes multi-cloud billing and spend management across AWS, Azure and GCP. Confirm billing consolidation, discounts, rebates and invoicing arrangements for the specific account.

chunks.title: What information is needed for a cloud consultation?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Commercial Question: What information is needed for a cloud consultation? Answer: Useful inputs include cloud providers, workload inventory, current spend, architecture, performance concerns, governance needs and desired outcomes. Do not share credentials in a public form.

chunks.title: What happens after cloud migration is completed?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Commercial Question: What happens after cloud migration is completed? Answer: Post-migration work may include validation, monitoring, documentation, knowledge transfer, cost review and operational handover. Ongoing operations depend on the agreed service scope.

chunks.title: Can Cache Digitech support cloud exit planning?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Commercial Question: Can Cache Digitech support cloud exit planning? Answer: A cloud exit plan considers data export, application dependencies, proprietary services, licensing, network design, contracts and migration testing. Confirm whether this advisory work is in scope.

chunks.title: How can I request a cloud architecture review?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Commercial Question: How can I request a cloud architecture review? Answer: Share business goals, current cloud/on-premises footprint, workloads, security constraints, performance issues and timeline through the official contact route.

chunks.title: What is the difference between public and private cloud?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Technical Question: What is the difference between public and private cloud? Answer: Public cloud services are delivered by a cloud provider; private cloud is dedicated to one organization. Selection depends on workload, control, security, performance and cost.

chunks.title: How should databases be migrated to cloud?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Technical Question: How should databases be migrated to cloud? Answer: Consider engine compatibility, data volume, replication, consistency, downtime tolerance, application connectivity, security and recovery. Confirm supported source and target databases.

chunks.title: How should cloud cost anomalies be handled?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Technical Question: How should cloud cost anomalies be handled? Answer: Define spend baselines, alert thresholds and investigation workflows. Distinguish legitimate demand changes from misconfiguration, unexpected data transfer or unauthorized use.

chunks.title: How should cloud workloads be validated after migration?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Technical Question: How should cloud workloads be validated after migration? Answer: Test functionality, data integrity, performance, security, integrations, monitoring, backup and user acceptance against criteria agreed before cutover.

chunks.title: What should be considered when adopting managed cloud services?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Technical Question: What should be considered when adopting managed cloud services? Answer: Define covered accounts, workloads, service hours, monitoring, change authority, escalation, reporting, security responsibilities and commercial terms.

chunks.title: How should cloud operating costs be forecast?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Technical Question: How should cloud operating costs be forecast? Answer: Use historical billing, workload growth, seasonality, pricing models, commitments, storage and data-transfer estimates. Revisit forecasts as usage changes.

chunks.title: What is cloud compliance evidence?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Technical Question: What is cloud compliance evidence? Answer: It is documented information showing how selected controls are implemented and monitored. Evidence requirements depend on the framework, architecture and audit scope.

chunks.title: How should cloud operations be handed over?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Technical Question: How should cloud operations be handed over? Answer: Provide architecture records, runbooks, monitoring, access procedures, known issues, escalation paths and knowledge-transfer sessions.

chunks.title: What is a cloud workload recovery test?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Technical Question: What is a cloud workload recovery test? Answer: A recovery test validates whether workloads and data can be restored within agreed recovery objectives. Record results, issues and remediation actions.

chunks.title: How can cloud performance be optimized?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Technical Question: How can cloud performance be optimized? Answer: Measure workload latency, throughput, utilization, dependencies and user experience, then test changes against agreed performance and resilience requirements.

chunks.title: What should be included in a cloud governance dashboard?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Cloud Topic: Technical Question: What should be included in a cloud governance dashboard? Answer: Potential measures include resource inventory, policy compliance, spend by owner, anomalies, security findings, utilization and unresolved actions.

chunks.title: What data and AI services does Cache Digitech offer?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: Data strategy Question: What data and AI services does Cache Digitech offer? Answer: Cache Digitech describes data analytics and AI capabilities, including data-driven insights and predictive dashboards. Its cloud page also references customized LLMs, RAG pipelines and agentic workflows; confirm current scope.

chunks.title: What is an AI readiness assessment?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI readiness Question: What is an AI readiness assessment? Answer: It evaluates business use cases, data quality and access, architecture, skills, security, governance and expected value to prioritize feasible AI initiatives.

chunks.title: How should an enterprise select an AI use case?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI strategy Question: How should an enterprise select an AI use case? Answer: Prioritize a clear business problem, measurable outcome, accessible data, manageable risk, accountable owner and realistic production path.

chunks.title: What is a data lake?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: Data platforms Question: What is a data lake? Answer: A data lake stores large volumes of structured, semi-structured and unstructured data. Governance, metadata, access controls and quality practices are essential.

chunks.title: What is a data warehouse?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: Data platforms Question: What is a data warehouse? Answer: A data warehouse organizes curated data for reporting and analytics, typically using defined schemas and quality controls.

chunks.title: What is a lakehouse architecture?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: Data platforms Question: What is a lakehouse architecture? Answer: A lakehouse combines aspects of data lakes and data warehouses to support varied data workloads with shared governance and management.

chunks.title: What is data integration?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: Data engineering Question: What is data integration? Answer: Data integration combines information from different systems using methods such as batch pipelines, APIs, streaming or replication, depending on freshness and reliability needs.

chunks.title: What is master data management?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: Data engineering Question: What is master data management? Answer: Master data management creates consistent, governed records for key entities such as customers, products or suppliers across systems.

chunks.title: What is data lineage?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: Data governance Question: What is data lineage? Answer: Data lineage records where data originated, how it changed and where it is consumed, supporting impact analysis, troubleshooting and auditability.

chunks.title: How is data quality assessed?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: Data quality Question: How is data quality assessed? Answer: Common dimensions include accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, validity and uniqueness. Rules should reflect the business use of the data.

chunks.title: How can duplicate or inconsistent data be reduced?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: Data quality Question: How can duplicate or inconsistent data be reduced? Answer: Use data standards, validation rules, matching logic, ownership and remediation workflows tailored to source systems and the risks of incorrect merges.

chunks.title: What is data governance?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: Data governance Question: What is data governance? Answer: Data governance defines ownership, policies, access, quality standards, metadata and lifecycle controls for data.

chunks.title: How should access to sensitive datasets be controlled?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: Data governance Question: How should access to sensitive datasets be controlled? Answer: Apply least-privilege access, role-based permissions, data classification, encryption, audit logging and periodic access reviews.

chunks.title: What is a KPI dashboard?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: Analytics Question: What is a KPI dashboard? Answer: A KPI dashboard presents selected business measures with definitions, trends and context. Metrics should have clear ownership and consistent calculations.

chunks.title: How can predictive analytics help a business?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: Analytics Question: How can predictive analytics help a business? Answer: Predictive analytics uses data to estimate likely outcomes, such as demand or risk. Usefulness depends on data quality, validation and operational integration.

chunks.title: What is real-time analytics?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: Analytics Question: What is real-time analytics? Answer: Real-time analytics processes data with low latency so teams can act on recent events. Its value depends on how quickly decisions must be made.

chunks.title: What is generative AI?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: Generative AI Question: What is generative AI? Answer: Generative AI uses models to produce content such as text, code or summaries. Enterprise use requires accuracy evaluation, privacy, security and human review.

chunks.title: What is a large language model (LLM)?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: Generative AI Question: What is a large language model (LLM)? Answer: An LLM is trained on large amounts of text and can support tasks such as summarization, extraction and question answering. Outputs can be incorrect.

chunks.title: What is Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: RAG Question: What is Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)? Answer: RAG retrieves relevant information from approved sources and provides it as context to a generative model. It can improve grounding but does not eliminate errors.

chunks.title: How can an enterprise chatbot answer from internal documents?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: RAG Question: How can an enterprise chatbot answer from internal documents? Answer: A common design indexes approved documents, retrieves relevant passages, applies access controls and generates grounded responses. Permissions, freshness and evaluation must be designed.

chunks.title: What is an enterprise knowledge engine?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: Knowledge engines Question: What is an enterprise knowledge engine? Answer: It helps users discover and query information across approved documents or systems, often using indexing, retrieval, metadata and natural-language interfaces.

chunks.title: How should AI hallucinations be managed?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI quality Question: How should AI hallucinations be managed? Answer: Use grounded retrieval, evaluations, citations where possible, human review and escalation for unsupported questions. No single technique eliminates all hallucinations.

chunks.title: How should an LLM be evaluated before production?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI evaluation Question: How should an LLM be evaluated before production? Answer: Evaluate task accuracy, groundedness, safety, latency, cost, robustness, privacy and representative test cases, then monitor after release.

chunks.title: What is prompt injection?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI security Question: What is prompt injection? Answer: Prompt injection attempts to manipulate a model through untrusted instructions. Defences include separating instructions from data, limiting tool permissions and testing attack scenarios.

chunks.title: How can enterprise data be protected when using AI models?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI privacy Question: How can enterprise data be protected when using AI models? Answer: Review data handling, retention, access control, encryption, logging, training settings and deployment location for the chosen model and hosting arrangement.

chunks.title: Can AI run in a private or controlled environment?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: Private AI Question: Can AI run in a private or controlled environment? Answer: Deployment options depend on model, infrastructure, licensing and operational requirements. The solution team must confirm which private or customer-controlled models are supported.

chunks.title: What is fine-tuning?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: Fine-tuning Question: What is fine-tuning? Answer: Fine-tuning further trains a model on curated examples to adapt behaviour to a task. It differs from RAG, which supplies retrieved context at inference time.

chunks.title: When should an enterprise use RAG versus fine-tuning?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: Fine-tuning Question: When should an enterprise use RAG versus fine-tuning? Answer: RAG is often suitable for current or source-specific information; fine-tuning may help with consistent task behaviour. Select by evaluating the use case.

chunks.title: What is an AI agent?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI agents Question: What is an AI agent? Answer: An AI agent uses a model to interpret a goal, select actions and interact with approved tools within defined permissions. Enterprise agents need guardrails and monitoring.

chunks.title: What is an agentic workflow?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI agents Question: What is an agentic workflow? Answer: An agentic workflow coordinates model-driven steps, tools and decisions to complete a task. Define permitted actions, failure handling, approvals and audit logs.

chunks.title: How can AI agents integrate with enterprise applications?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI agents Question: How can AI agents integrate with enterprise applications? Answer: Integration commonly uses APIs or controlled tool interfaces with scoped credentials and input/output validation. Test permissions, reliability and data exposure.

chunks.title: How should AI agent permissions be managed?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI agents Question: How should AI agent permissions be managed? Answer: Use least-privilege identities, narrowly scoped tools, approval gates for high-impact actions, secret management, logging and periodic reviews.

chunks.title: What is human-in-the-loop AI?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: Human oversight Question: What is human-in-the-loop AI? Answer: It requires people to review or approve selected outputs or actions, especially where errors have significant consequences or accountability requires human judgement.

chunks.title: What is MLOps?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI operations Question: What is MLOps? Answer: MLOps applies engineering practices to model lifecycle activities such as data/model versioning, testing, deployment, monitoring and retraining.

chunks.title: What is LLMOps?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI operations Question: What is LLMOps? Answer: LLMOps covers operational practices for LLM applications, including prompt/model versioning, evaluations, monitoring, latency, cost, safety and retrieval quality.

chunks.title: How should model drift be monitored?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI operations Question: How should model drift be monitored? Answer: Monitor changes in input data, output quality, user feedback and business outcomes against a baseline. Define thresholds and remediation actions.

chunks.title: What is GPU infrastructure used for?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI infrastructure Question: What is GPU infrastructure used for? Answer: GPUs accelerate parallel workloads such as model training, inference and scientific computing. Sizing depends on model, concurrency, memory, latency and utilization.

chunks.title: How should GPU capacity be planned?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI infrastructure Question: How should GPU capacity be planned? Answer: Estimate workload size, model memory, concurrency, throughput, utilization, network and storage needs, power/cooling and growth; benchmark representative workloads.

chunks.title: What is responsible AI governance?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI governance Question: What is responsible AI governance? Answer: It defines accountability, permitted use, risk assessment, evaluation, human oversight, transparency and monitoring across the AI lifecycle.

chunks.title: How can sensitive data be kept out of model prompts?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI privacy Question: How can sensitive data be kept out of model prompts? Answer: Use data classification, access controls, redaction where appropriate, approved connectors and prompt inspection. Do not send confidential data to unapproved endpoints.

chunks.title: What is an AI proof of concept (PoC)?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI delivery Question: What is an AI proof of concept (PoC)? Answer: A PoC tests feasibility and value against agreed success criteria using representative data. It should consider risks, costs and a decision path to production.

chunks.title: What is required to move an AI pilot into production?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI delivery Question: What is required to move an AI pilot into production? Answer: Production readiness includes security review, data permissions, evaluation, integration, reliability, monitoring, cost controls, support ownership and incident procedures.

chunks.title: How should AI project success be measured?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI delivery Question: How should AI project success be measured? Answer: Use use-case-specific measures such as task accuracy, processing time, adoption, error rates, cost per task and business impact with a defined baseline.

chunks.title: Can Cache Digitech build custom AI solutions?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI commercial Question: Can Cache Digitech build custom AI solutions? Answer: The website references data analytics, customized LLMs, RAG pipelines and agentic workflows. Confirm current platforms, deployment models and engagement scope.

chunks.title: Which information should I share to discuss an AI use case?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI commercial Question: Which information should I share to discuss an AI use case? Answer: Share the business problem, intended users, data sources, current systems, desired outcome, risk constraints and timeline. Do not submit confidential data through a general form.

chunks.title: Can AI be integrated with existing business systems?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI integration Question: Can AI be integrated with existing business systems? Answer: Integration may use APIs, connectors or data pipelines, subject to the target system's capabilities, permissions and security requirements.

chunks.title: How is enterprise AI cost estimated?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI economics Question: How is enterprise AI cost estimated? Answer: Costs may include model usage, compute/GPU, data engineering, storage, integration, evaluation, security and operations. Estimate using expected workload volume and tests.

chunks.title: How should AI outputs be reviewed before use?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI risk Question: How should AI outputs be reviewed before use? Answer: Review requirements depend on error impact. Use validation rules, evidence, human approval, audit trails and escalation for uncertain or high-impact cases.

chunks.title: What is the difference between a chatbot and an AI agent?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Data & AI Topic: AI architecture Question: What is the difference between a chatbot and an AI agent? Answer: A chatbot primarily interacts through conversation; an AI agent may also plan steps and use tools to act toward a goal. Actual capabilities depend on design and permissions.

chunks.title: What infrastructure services does Cache Digitech offer?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Service overview Question: What infrastructure services does Cache Digitech offer? Answer: The website describes infrastructure consulting, design, build, operation and management, including servers, storage, networking, virtualization, cloud integration and data-centre migration.

chunks.title: What is an infrastructure assessment?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Assessment Question: What is an infrastructure assessment? Answer: It reviews assets, dependencies, capacity, performance, lifecycle, risks and operations to identify gaps and modernization priorities.

chunks.title: What is infrastructure capacity planning?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Capacity Question: What is infrastructure capacity planning? Answer: It compares current utilization and performance with forecast demand to identify future compute, storage, network or facility needs.

chunks.title: What is a technology refresh?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Lifecycle Question: What is a technology refresh? Answer: A refresh replaces or upgrades ageing hardware or software to address supportability, performance, security, capacity or lifecycle concerns.

chunks.title: What is the role of enterprise servers?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Compute Question: What is the role of enterprise servers? Answer: Enterprise servers provide compute for applications, databases, virtualization, analytics and other workloads. Selection depends on performance, availability and support requirements.

chunks.title: How should server sizing be determined?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Compute Question: How should server sizing be determined? Answer: Use workload profiles, CPU/memory utilization, peak demand, growth, availability, software requirements and performance tests.

chunks.title: What is server virtualization?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Virtualization Question: What is server virtualization? Answer: It uses a hypervisor or platform to run multiple virtual machines on physical hosts. It requires capacity planning, licensing, security and high-availability design.

chunks.title: What is the difference between a virtual machine and a container?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Virtualization Question: What is the difference between a virtual machine and a container? Answer: A virtual machine includes a guest OS on virtualized hardware; a container packages an application and dependencies while sharing the host kernel.

chunks.title: What is hyperconverged infrastructure (HCI)?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: HCI Question: What is hyperconverged infrastructure (HCI)? Answer: HCI combines compute, storage and virtualization management into an integrated platform. Suitability depends on scale, performance, resilience and licensing.

chunks.title: What is the difference between SAN and NAS?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Storage Question: What is the difference between SAN and NAS? Answer: SAN provides block-level storage, often for servers and databases. NAS provides file-level access. Selection depends on application and performance needs.

chunks.title: How should enterprise storage capacity be planned?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Storage Question: How should enterprise storage capacity be planned? Answer: Plan usable capacity, growth, performance, protection overhead, snapshots, replication, retention and recovery needs.

chunks.title: What is storage tiering?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Storage Question: What is storage tiering? Answer: Storage tiering places data on different storage types based on performance, access frequency, cost and retention needs.

chunks.title: How can storage performance be troubleshot?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Storage Question: How can storage performance be troubleshot? Answer: Review latency, IOPS, throughput, queue depth, cache, host paths, network and workload patterns across the application, server and storage layers.

chunks.title: What is enterprise network design?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Networking Question: What is enterprise network design? Answer: It defines connectivity, segmentation, routing, capacity, resilience, security and management across sites and workloads.

chunks.title: What is network segmentation?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Networking Question: What is network segmentation? Answer: It divides an environment into zones with controlled communication, helping limit exposure and lateral movement when paired with suitable access controls.

chunks.title: What is software-defined networking (SDN)?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Networking Question: What is software-defined networking (SDN)? Answer: SDN enables policy-driven network management through software. Suitability depends on the platform, use case and existing network design.

chunks.title: How should branch or remote-site infrastructure be managed?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Branch infrastructure Question: How should branch or remote-site infrastructure be managed? Answer: Standardized configurations, secure connectivity, centralized monitoring, patching, asset inventory and remote support can simplify distributed operations.

chunks.title: What is data-centre modernization?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Data centre Question: What is data-centre modernization? Answer: It assesses and updates compute, storage, networking, virtualization, management and resilience to meet current requirements.

chunks.title: What should be included in a data-centre migration plan?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Data centre Question: What should be included in a data-centre migration plan? Answer: Include inventory, dependency mapping, target design, sequencing, backup, change windows, testing, cutover, rollback and post-migration validation.

chunks.title: Can a data-centre migration be completed with zero downtime?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Data centre Question: Can a data-centre migration be completed with zero downtime? Answer: Downtime depends on application architecture, replication, dependencies and cutover method. Any zero-downtime claim must be assessed and tested per workload.

chunks.title: What is high availability?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Availability Question: What is high availability? Answer: High availability reduces service interruption through redundancy, failover and elimination of single points of failure, supported by testing and operations.

chunks.title: What is disaster recovery?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Recovery Question: What is disaster recovery? Answer: Disaster recovery restores systems and data after disruption. Plans should define RTO, RPO, dependencies, runbooks, ownership and regular tests.

chunks.title: What are RTO and RPO?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Recovery Question: What are RTO and RPO? Answer: RTO is the target time to restore a service. RPO is the target maximum data loss measured in time. Both should be agreed and tested.

chunks.title: How should backups be designed?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Backup Question: How should backups be designed? Answer: Consider scope, frequency, retention, isolation, encryption, access controls and restoration testing. Successful backup jobs alone do not prove recoverability.

chunks.title: What is a private cloud?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Private cloud Question: What is a private cloud? Answer: A private cloud provides cloud-like resource provisioning in an environment dedicated to one organization. Design depends on automation, governance and operating model.

chunks.title: How can on-premises infrastructure integrate with public cloud?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Hybrid Question: How can on-premises infrastructure integrate with public cloud? Answer: Plan connectivity, identity, monitoring, data movement, security policies, workload dependencies and operational ownership.

chunks.title: What is infrastructure monitoring?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Monitoring Question: What is infrastructure monitoring? Answer: It tracks health and performance of servers, storage, networks and related services through metrics, logs and alerts tied to owners and runbooks.

chunks.title: What is proactive infrastructure management?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Operations Question: What is proactive infrastructure management? Answer: It uses health checks, trend analysis, preventive maintenance, patch planning and capacity reviews to reduce avoidable disruptions.

chunks.title: How should infrastructure incidents be investigated?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Troubleshooting Question: How should infrastructure incidents be investigated? Answer: Correlate impact, timeline, monitoring data and recent changes; identify dependencies, mitigate safely and document root cause and corrective actions.

chunks.title: What is configuration management?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Configuration Question: What is configuration management? Answer: It maintains controlled records of system settings and changes, supporting consistency, troubleshooting and auditability.

chunks.title: How should firmware and patches be managed?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Patching Question: How should firmware and patches be managed? Answer: Use inventories, vendor advisories, risk prioritization, compatibility checks, maintenance windows, testing, backups and rollback plans.

chunks.title: What are infrastructure engineering services?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Engineering Question: What are infrastructure engineering services? Answer: They include designing, integrating and implementing components such as compute, storage, networks, virtualization and cloud connectivity.

chunks.title: What is system integration?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Integration Question: What is system integration? Answer: It connects technology components into a coherent environment, addressing compatibility, interfaces, identity, data flows, security and testing.

chunks.title: How should a new infrastructure solution be designed?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Design Question: How should a new infrastructure solution be designed? Answer: Start with workload requirements, current architecture, capacity, availability, security, compliance, supportability and growth, then document target design and acceptance criteria.

chunks.title: What is infrastructure documentation?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Documentation Question: What is infrastructure documentation? Answer: It records architecture, inventories, configurations, dependencies, support details, procedures and standards, with ownership and version control.

chunks.title: How can infrastructure technical debt be reduced?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Technical debt Question: How can infrastructure technical debt be reduced? Answer: Identify unsupported platforms, inconsistent configurations, manual processes and fragile dependencies; prioritize by risk, supportability, cost and feasibility.

chunks.title: How can server performance be improved?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Performance Question: How can server performance be improved? Answer: Measure CPU, memory, storage latency, network throughput and application behaviour under representative load, then address the actual bottleneck.

chunks.title: How should infrastructure scalability be designed?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Scalability Question: How should infrastructure scalability be designed? Answer: Use demand forecasts, modular architecture, automation and tested expansion procedures, including licensing, network, storage and support capacity.

chunks.title: How can infrastructure be hardened?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Hardening Question: How can infrastructure be hardened? Answer: Apply secure configuration baselines, least privilege, patching, segmentation, logging, vulnerability remediation and controlled administrative access.

chunks.title: How should privileged access to infrastructure be controlled?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Privileged access Question: How should privileged access to infrastructure be controlled? Answer: Use named accounts, strong authentication, least privilege, logging, periodic reviews and controlled emergency access.

Answer: The website describes infrastructure consulting, design, build and operation/management. Confirm equipment, implementation scope, responsibilities and support terms.

chunks.title: Can Cache Digitech support a mixed-vendor infrastructure environment?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Commercial Question: Can Cache Digitech support a mixed-vendor infrastructure environment? Answer: Support depends on technologies, versions, interoperability, access and contractual scope. Provide an inventory for compatibility review.

chunks.title: How is an infrastructure project scoped?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Commercial Question: How is an infrastructure project scoped? Answer: Scope depends on current-state findings, target architecture, equipment/software, dependencies, migration, testing, documentation and support.

chunks.title: What should I prepare before an infrastructure consultation?
chunks.text: FAQ Group: Infrastructure & Engineering Topic: Commercial Question: What should I prepare before an infrastructure consultation? Answer: Prepare a high-level inventory, workload needs, growth estimates, architecture, risks, lifecycle constraints and desired outcomes.
